skill.name: project-planner
skill.description: Generate structured software project plans with requirements, design specifications, and task breakdowns for AI-assisted implementation.
skill.summary: Create traceable project planning documents for software teams and AI coding agents.
skill.author: Dwsy

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline technical notation, and example deployment text. The only confirmed risk is intended local filesystem writing by the document generator, which can overwrite generated document filenames in a user-selected directory.

remediation.issue: Generated files can overwrite existing Markdown files in the selected output directory.
remediation.suggestion: Check whether requirements.md, design.md, or tasks.md already exist before writing, or add a --force flag for intentional overwrites.

remediation.issue: The generator writes to any path provided by --output.
remediation.suggestion: Normalize the output path, show the resolved destination before writing, and document that the script creates local files only.

remediation.issue: Example deployment templates include placeholder secrets such as database URLs and API keys.
remediation.suggestion: Label these values clearly as placeholders and avoid realistic credential formats in generated examples.

content.user_title: Plan Software Projects with Traceable Documents
content.value_statement: Software teams often start implementation before requirements, architecture, and tasks are clear. This skill creates structured planning documents that Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can use for focused delivery.
actual_capabilities: Creates requirements documents with user stories, acceptance criteria, and glossary sections.
Generates design documents with components, interfaces, data flows, and deployment notes.
Builds implementation plans with phases, tasks, dependencies, and requirement traceability.
Provides domain templates for common software project types and architecture patterns.
Includes a validator for checking completeness and consistency across planning documents.
limitations: Generated documents contain placeholders that users must review and complete.
The included generator writes local Markdown files and can overwrite matching filenames.
Architecture recommendations depend on the project details supplied by the user.
The skill does not build the software or verify deployed system behavior.

use_cases.title: Plan a new application
use_cases.description: Turn a product idea into requirements, design decisions, and an implementation task list before coding starts.

use_cases.title: Prepare AI coding work
use_cases.description: Create structured documents that give Claude, Codex, or Claude Code clear scope, interfaces, and task order.

use_cases.title: Standardize technical planning
use_cases.description: Use repeatable templates for requirements, architecture, validation checks, and milestone planning across projects.

prompt_templates.title: Start a simple project plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a new project idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a new web application for [target users]. Create requirements, a system design outline, and a first implementation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Define requirements from features
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the main features are known.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create requirements for [project name] with these features: [feature list]. Include user stories, acceptance criteria, and requirement IDs.

prompt_templates.title: Design architecture and boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the architecture for [project name]. Include components, data flows, integration points, interfaces, scope boundaries, and deployment assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a traceable delivery plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an implementation plan for [project name]. Map each task to requirements, components, dependencies, deliverables, and measurable success criteria.

output_examples.input: A user asks to plan a real-time chat application for small teams.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a requirements document, a design document with messaging components, and a phased task plan for authentication, rooms, messaging, and notifications.

output_examples.input: A developer has requirements but needs an architecture plan.
output_examples.output: The skill organizes components, data flows, interface contracts, failure handling, deployment assumptions, and performance targets into a design document.

output_examples.input: An engineering lead wants a delivery plan for an API service.
output_examples.output: The skill creates phases, task checklists, dependencies, requirement links, component ownership, and success criteria for implementation tracking.

best_practices: Provide target users, core features, technical preferences, and non-functional requirements before generating documents.
Review placeholders and replace them with project-specific facts before using the plan for implementation.
Validate that each task maps to a requirement and each requirement has testable acceptance criteria.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated templates as final specifications without human review.
Do not run the generator in a directory that already contains important files with the same output names.
Do not skip scope boundaries, integration points, or failure cases when asking for a plan.

faq.question: What documents does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates requirements, design, and implementation plan documents in Markdown format.

faq.question: Can I use it with an existing project?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the current goals, architecture, constraints, and gaps so the skill can update the planning documents.

faq.question: Does it write files automatically?
faq.answer: The included Python generator can write local Markdown files when run. The skill instructions can also be used without running scripts.

faq.question: Does it choose my technology stack?
faq.answer: It can suggest structure, but final stack choices should reflect your team, constraints, and deployment environment.

faq.question: How does it help AI coding agents?
faq.answer: It gives agents clear requirements, interfaces, task order, and acceptance criteria for more predictable implementation.

faq.question: Should I validate the generated documents?
faq.answer: Yes. Review all placeholders and run the included validator if you use the generated Markdown files.
